arxiv-2004-06029.title: Non-genetic inheritance restraint of cell-to-cell variation
arxiv-2004-06029.creator: Harsh Vashistha, Maryam Kohram, Hanna Salman
arxiv-2004-06029.description: Abstract Heterogeneity in physical and functional characteristics of cells (e.g. size, cycle time, growth rate, protein concentration) proliferates within an isogenic population due to stochasticity in intracellular biochemical processes and in the distribution of resources during divisions. Conversely, it is limited in part by the inheritance of cellular components between consecutive generations.

arxiv-2012-07342.title: Non-uniform ergodic properties of Hamiltonian flows with impacts Thanks: Research partially supported by the Narodowe Centrum Nauki Grant 2017/27/B/ST1/00078 and by ISF Grant 1208/16.
arxiv-2012-07342.creator: Krzysztof Frączek, Vered Rom-Kedar
arxiv-2012-07342.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Krzysztof Frączek, Vered Rom-Kedar. The ergodic properties of two uncoupled oscillators, a horizontal and vertical one, residing in a class of non rectangular star-shaped polygons with only vertical and horizontal boundaries and impacting elastically from its boundaries are studied. We prove that the iso-energy level sets topology changes non-trivially; the flow on level sets is always conjugated to a translation flow on a translation surface, yet, for some segments of partial energies the genus of the surface is strictly larger than one.

arxiv-2108-01490.title: Extending dynamic mode decomposition to data from multiple outputs
arxiv-2108-01490.creator: Nibodh Boddupalli
arxiv-2108-01490.description: Abstract System identification based on Koopman operator theory has grown in popularity recently. Spectral properties of the Koopman operator of a system were proven to relate to properties like invariant sets, stability, periodicity, etc. of the underlying system. Estimation of these spectral objects has become widely accessible with the numerous algorithms developed in recent years.

arxiv-2203-14669.title: Theory and Experiment of Dynamic Structure in Four-strategy Game An extended abstract has appeared in the 15th international conference on game theory and management (GTM2021), June 23 - 25, 2021 St. Petersburg, Russia. WZJ designed the research, ZSJ carried out the experiments and primer data analy
arxiv-2203-14669.creator: Wang Zhijian, Zhou Shujie, Yao Qinmei, Wang Yijia
arxiv-2203-14669.description: Abstract Game dynamics theory, as any field of science, the consistency of theory and experiment is essential. In the past 10 years, important progress has been made in the merging of the theory and experiment in this field, in which dynamics cycle is the presentation.

arxiv-2204-03590.title: Reliability of the Ginzburg-Landau Theory in the BCS-BEC Crossover by Including Gaussian Fluctuations for 3D Attractive Fermions
arxiv-2204-03590.creator: F. Pascucci 1 , A. Perali 1 , and L. Salasnich 2
arxiv-2204-03590.description: Abstract We calculate the parameters of the Ginzburg–Landau (GL) equation of a three-dimensional attractive Fermi gas around the superfluid critical temperature. We compare different levels of approximation throughout the Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) to the Bose–Einstein Condensate (BEC) regime. We show that the inclusion of Gaussian fluctuations strongly modifies the values of the Ginzburg–Landau parameters approaching the BEC regime of the crossover.

arxiv-2206-08391.title: Quantum Anomaly Detection for Collider Physics
arxiv-2206-08391.creator: Sulaiman Alvi, a,b, Christian Bauer, b, and Benjamin Nachman, b,c
arxiv-2206-08391.description: Abstract Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is an exciting tool that has received significant recent attention due in part to advances in quantum computing hardware. While there is currently no formal guarantee that QML is superior to classical ML for relevant problems, there have been many claims of an empirical advantage with high energy physics datasets.

arxiv-2208-00403.title: SG-Based Analysis of LEO Satellite-Relayed Communication Systems
arxiv-2208-00403.creator: Yanbo Cao, Derui Gao, Jingyu Xu
arxiv-2208-00403.description: Abstract Due to their low latency, high capacity, and seamless worldwide coverage, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are essential to the equal access network. Stochastic geometry (SG) is an appropriate method for such a large and irregular system. The SG model can effectively assess and estimate the performance of the network as well as handle the growing network scale.

arxiv-2410-04833.title: Multimodal Fusion Strategies for Mapping Biophysical Landscape Features
arxiv-2410-04833.creator: Lucia Gordon, Nico Lang, Catherine Ressijac, Andrew Davies
arxiv-2410-04833.description: Abstract Multimodal aerial data are used to monitor natural systems, and machine learning can significantly accelerate the classification of landscape features within such imagery to benefit ecology and conservation. It remains under-explored, however, how these multiple modalities ought to be fused in a deep learning model.

arxiv-2410-10216.title: Neural Quasiprobabilistic Likelihood Ratio Estimation with Negatively Weighted Data
arxiv-2410-10216.creator: Matthew Drnevich*, Stephen Jiggins*, Judith Katzy, Kyle Cranmer
arxiv-2410-10216.description: Abstract Motivated by real-world situations found in high energy particle physics, we consider a generalisation of the likelihood-ratio estimation task to a quasiprobabilistic setting where probability densities can be negative. By extension, this framing also applies to importance sampling in a setting where the importance weights can be negative.

arxiv-2501-05150.title: Heat transport model for the transition between scaling regimes in quasistatic and full magnetoconvection
arxiv-2501-05150.creator: Matthew McCormack, Andrei Teimurazov, Olga Shishkina, Moritz Linkmann
arxiv-2501-05150.description: Abstract In magnetoconvection, the flow is governed by the interplay between gravitational buoyancy and the Lorentz force, with one of these forces dominating in different regimes. In this paper, we develop a model with a single adjustable parameter that accurately captures the smooth transition from a buoyancy-dominated regime to one dominated by the Lorentz force.

arxiv-2511-07436.title: Analysing Environmental Efficiency in AI for X-Ray Diagnosis
arxiv-2511-07436.creator: Liam Kearns
arxiv-2511-07436.description: Abstract The integration of AI tools into medical applications has aimed to improve the efficiency of diagnosis. The emergence of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and Claude, has expanded this integration even further. Because of LLM versatility and ease of use through APIs, these larger models are often utilised even though smaller, custom models can be used instead.

arxiv-2511-13576.title: Exploring the Effectiveness of Google Play Store’s Privacy Transparency Channels
arxiv-2511-13576.creator: Anhao Xiang \ORCID 0000-0002-8850-8583, Weiping Pei \ORCID 0000-0002-6831-2313, Chuan Yue \ORCID 0000-0002-6095-4768
arxiv-2511-13576.description: Abstract With the requirements and emphases on privacy transparency placed by regulations such as GDPR and CCPA, the Google Play Store requires Android developers to more responsibly communicate their apps’ privacy practices to potential users by providing the proper information via the data safety , privacy policy , and permission manifest privacy transparency channels.

arxiv-2602-06612.title: HYDRA: Unearthing “Black Swan” Vulnerabilities in LEO Satellite Networks
arxiv-2602-06612.creator: Bintao Yuan, Mingsheng Tang, Binbin Ge, Hongbin Luo1, Zijie yan
arxiv-2602-06612.description: Abstract As Low Earth Orbit (LEO) become mega-constellations critical infrastructure, attacks targeting them have grown in number and range. The security analysis of LEO constellations faces a fundamental paradigm gap: traditional topology-centric methods fail to capture systemic risks arising from dynamic load imbalances and high-order dependencies, which can transform localized failures into network-wide cascades.

pmc-10503083.title: Lifestyle behaviors and stress are risk factors for overweight and obesity in healthcare workers: a cross-sectional survey
pmc-10503083.creator: Xinyue Guo, Shaoqing Gong, Ying Chen, Xiaohui Hou, Tong Sun, Jianqiang Wen, Zhiyao Wang, Jingyang He, Xuezhu Sun, Sufang Wang, Xue Feng, Xiangyang Tian
pmc-10503083.description: BackgroundOverweight and obesity have become major public health concerns worldwide. Persistent stress can activate the human hypothalamic‒pituitary‒adrenal axis (HPA) and increase the intake of “self-rewarding food”, thereby raising the incidence of obesity. Health care workers (HCWs) experience higher workloads and mental stress than workers in many other industries, which may put them at increased risk for overweight/obesity.

pmc-10660795.title: Single‐cell sequencing of multi‐region resolves geospatial architecture and therapeutic target of endothelial cells in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-10660795.creator: Jiacheng Dai, Xiaoxiang Xi, Zidong Liu, Weicheng Wu, Sibo Zhu, Xiaoyang Zhang, Yuwei Huang, Jiayue Meng, Liyun Yuan, Chen Suo, Jiangli Xue, Ziyu Yuan, Ming Lv, Weimin Ye, Li Jin, Guoqing Zhang, Xingdong Chen
pmc-10660795.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). which is characterized by rapid invasion and metastasis and has a poor clinical outcome. 1 Recently, the genetic landscape 2 and single‐cell atlas 3 , 4 of ESCC have been unveiled; however, the vascular heterogeneity in ESCC remained unknown. Our study fully characterized the endothelial cells in ESCC, which may have implications for the development of anti‐angiogenic therapies (AATs) in ESCC.

pmc-11496986.title: Preference Signals and Interview Invitations: Insight Into Recent Updates to the Oto‐HNS Residency Application Process
pmc-11496986.creator: Radhika Duggal, Kyra Osborne, Alan Kominsky, William S Tierney
pmc-11496986.description: ObjectiveWhile students in the 2023 Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery (Oto‐HNS) residency match were allowed 7 preference signals, this number increased to 25 for the 2024 match with the goal of reducing the overall application volume. We sought to understand the impact of this change to application volume and interview patterns.Study DesignCross‐sectional survey.

pmc-11546816.title: Closing the gap: proposing a socio-ecological framework to make cancer clinical trials more accessible, equitable, and acceptable to adolescents and young adults
pmc-11546816.creator: Zeba Ahmad, Vinayak Venkataraman, Michaela Markwart, Annah N Abrams, Jennifer S Temel, Giselle K Perez
pmc-11546816.description: This commentary focuses on what would make cancer clinical trials more accessible, equitable, and acceptable to adolescents and young adults. Optimizing AYA CCT participation with a socio-ecological approach Each year, 85 000 adolescents and young adults (AYAs, 15-39 years old) are diagnosed with cancer in the United States.

pmc-11556574.title: Key stakeholder perspectives on delivery of vaccination services in Quebec community pharmacies
pmc-11556574.creator: Alexandre Chadi, Daniel J. G. Thirion, Nancy M. Waite, Pierre-Marie David
pmc-11556574.description: Background:Undervaccination is a public health issue that disproportionately affects underserved populations. Pharmacists are accessible health care professionals who have the potential to better reach communities. The aim of this study is to understand how organizational obstacles influence the pharmacist’s ability to meet underserved clients’ vaccination needs in community pharmacy.Methods:We conducted semi-structured interviews with key stakeholders in Quebec.

pmc-12370922.title: Mapping Alzheimer’s disease pathology using free water through integrated analysis of plasma biomarkers, microstructural DTI metrics, and macrostructural MRI measures
pmc-12370922.creator: Bo-Hyun Kim, Daeun Shin, Sung Hoon Kang, Hyemin Jang, Jihwan Yun, YuHyun Park, Henrik Zetterberg, Kaj Blennow, Fernando Gonzalez-Ortiz, Nicholas J Ashton, Sung Tae Kim, Hee Jin Kim, Duk L Na, Jun Pyo Kim, Sang Won Seo
pmc-12370922.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau pathologies that drive neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. Free water (FW), a diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metric reflecting extracellular fluid changes, has emerged as a sensitive marker of neuroinflammation. This study examined the role of FW in AD and its associations with plasma biomarkers, brain structural measures, and cognitive decline.

pmc-12834974.title: Temperature and composition effects on fresh and hardened properties of slag-fly ash-silica fume alkali-activated grouting materials
pmc-12834974.creator: Yu-chen Qian, Li Zhang, Wei-guo Qiao, Yan-zhi Li, Yue Wu, Yun-rui Zhao
pmc-12834974.description: Growing concerns over carbon emissions from traditional cement have intensified interest in alkali-activated materials (AAM) as sustainable alternatives. In grouting applications, key performance parameters such as strength, fluidity, viscosity, setting time, and bleeding rate are strongly influenced by both material composition and curing temperature.

pmc-13263753.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of microsurgery and radiosurgery outcomes in low-grade cerebral arteriovenous malformations: Obliteration rates, morbidity, and mortality
pmc-13263753.creator: Setyo Widi Nugroho, Nadya Zaragita, Aryandhito Widhi Nugroho, Fabianto Santoso, Sayyid Abdil Hakam Perkasa, Adhitya Syahada, Theresia Meiske Laura Siscawati Wayne
pmc-13263753.description: IntroductionLow-grade cerebral arteriovenous malformations (LGCAVMs) are treated with microsurgery according to Spetzler-Martin (SM) grade. Radiosurgery is an emerging treatment for LGCAVMs. Existing comparative evidence is mostly from retrospective, non-randomized cohorts, limiting direct comparison between treatments.Research questionThis study compared the outcomes of microsurgery and radiosurgery for LGCAVMs.Material and Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-13280026.title: Baseline Reaction Time and Subsequent Sport-Related Concussion Risk Among Female Youth Soccer Players
pmc-13280026.creator: Katherine Smulligan, Landon Lempke, Rebekah Mannix, Kristin Whitney, Paul Berkner, Jessie Oldham, William Meehan
pmc-13280026.description: Background:Slow reaction time is associated with sustaining sport-related musculoskeletal injuries.1,2 However, it is unknown whether slow reaction time may also identify individuals at risk of a sport-related concussion. Our purpose was to investigate the association between baseline reaction time and subsequent sport-related concussion (SRC) among junior high female soccer players.

pmc-13344296.title: Stiffness-tunable oral nanoparticles facilitate damaged islet β cell restoration for diabetes treatment
pmc-13344296.creator: Wenyan She, Xiaojuan Jiang, Siying Deng, Luyuan Hu, Chenxi Huang, Lin Hou
pmc-13344296.description: Diabetes mellitus remains a global health challenge, as current insulin-based therapies merely control blood glucose without restoring islet β cell function, leaving patients dependent on lifelong medication and vulnerable to hypoglycemia. Antioxidant drugs hold promise for islet β cell repair but are limited by poor gastrointestinal transportation and insufficient pancreatic targetability.

pmc-13507996.title: Molecular Mechanism of the SepF N‑Terminal Conformational Switch in Ring Assembly and Membrane Anchoring
pmc-13507996.creator: Wenjing Liu, Chang Zhang, Mojie Duan, Meng Yao, Ziwei Chang, Jun Yang
pmc-13507996.description: Septum-forming protein (SepF) self-assembles into ring-shaped structures during bacterial cell division, acting as a bridge that anchors the Z-ring to the cell membrane and thereby facilitates membrane remodeling and constriction. In this study, we elucidate how salt ions regulate the ring assembly of SepF and its membrane anchoring using solid-state NMR (ssNMR) spectroscopy in combination with biochemical methods.
